title: Teaching Marian to swing
summary: He told her the key to jazz is the beat, and recalls Leonard Feather's three strikes against her.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I'm wondering if it would be fair to say then in view of what I've just listened to that you have a great deal to do with Marian's becoming a jazz pianist?

Well she liked jazz all her life you know. And she asked me what to do, what to do? And I said, I just kept telling her panning, look, there's only one thing that you can do because you have the facility of the instrument and you're a fine musician and that is that beat, that beat. You've got to learn how to swing. And just to hold that beat right steady where it is you know. It's called, it's time you know.
And as we talked before, it's the Afro beat it's the tom-toms......
You've got to feel it before you play jazz.

You have to feel it before you play jazz and you've got to feel it so the only thing I can say is just feel it, just feel that time, feel that rhythm, that beat, feel that beat. And once you get the feel of it you've got it because you have all the other facilities.
You can make all the distortions you want but you've got to go back to that, yes.
You've got to come back to that basic beat, that rhythm is your thing, is the thing. Because you have all your harmonies and everything else.

So she just kept doing it and that's a girl that really did it. And I'm telling you, you know, I don't know how because, who was it, Leonard Feather? He said poor Marian has got three strikes against her before she even starts being a jazz musician. And that is she's British, she's white...
